html:
SMTO-CMP-0017 — SMTO can't find the final result of a long-running job

GUID: 53dacc71-234e-4c30-8765-bb2a754076a2
Slug: completion-invalid-job-receipt
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The task relies on a long-running job SMTO started earlier, but SMTO can't find that job's final result, or the result doesn't match the job. So it can't confirm the task is done. Work so far is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's steps for the long-running job and whether it finished, failed or is still waiting. SMTO needs that job's final result before it can confirm the task.
  2. If you can, check the job's real outcome on the computer or service where it ran. The job may have finished even though its final result isn't linked correctly.
  3. Select Resume, or in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task ask SMTO to check the job's status rather than start it again, then select Continue. Checking the job gets its final result without running the job twice.
  4. Don't select Restart task. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so the job could run a second time.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply reports the job's final result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't start the same job again yourself until you know whether the first one finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A cited durable job has no terminal receipt, or its terminal receipt does not supersede and correlate to the original job_id (reason invalid_job_receipt).

What this means

  • A cited durable job lacks a terminal receipt or the receipt does not supersede/correlate to its original job ID. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A cited durable job lacks a terminal receipt or the receipt does not supersede/correlate to its original job ID.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect authoritative job state, terminal receipt ID and supersedes/job_id correlation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the job's state and terminal_receipt_id, and the job's _result receipt for a supersedes entry and data.job_id matching the original job ID (evidence_job and resolve_evidence in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py). Reconcile the job through manage_job so it resolves to a valid terminal receipt, then cite that receipt; do not relaunch the job.
  • Inspect the authoritative job state and use a valid terminal job receipt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact original job resolves to a valid eligible terminal receipt.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
